sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-state tax or regulatory subdivisions applicable to SCSp formation)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic-derived unitary jurisdiction; French code-based commercial law and Benelux unification, with strong EU secondary law influence)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: BLEU–China Bilateral Investment Protection Treaty (signed 22 November 2005, in force 1 December 2009)
Luxembourg–United States Income and Capital Tax Treaty (1996, as amended by Protocols of 2004 and 2009)
Luxembourg–China Double Taxation Agreement (signed 14 March 1994, as amended by the Protocol of 16 November 2019)
Luxembourg–United Kingdom Double Taxation Agreement (2017, operative post-Brexit)
Luxembourg–France Double Taxation Agreement (1958, as amended, including the 2006 supplementary protocol)
EU–Japan Economic Partnership Agreement (2019) and EU–Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA, provisionally applied 2017)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Articles 1023-1 to 1023-16 for the SCSp); Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended, notably by the Laws of 17 July 2020 and 21 December 2023; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) together with its Grand-Ducal Regulation of 15 January 2019; CSSF Regulation No. 12-02 of 14 December 2012; CSSF Circular 21/780 (AML/CFT expectations for professionals); Luxembourg Criminal Code, Articles 506-1 et seq. (money-laundering predicates and sanctions).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national identity card of every Ultimate Beneficial Owner and of each proposed General Partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport/national registrar authority of the document's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille under the 1961 Convention issued by the competent authority of the issuing state; full consular legalization via the Embassy/Consulate of Luxembourg in the issuing state where that state is not a Hague member

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / official corporate extract of any corporate General Partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official Trade or Commercial Register of the corporate partner's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or, failing Hague membership, consular legalization through the Luxembourg diplomatic post in the jurisdiction of issuance

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency, register of directors and shareholders of any corporate General Partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered agent or corporate service provider duly licensed in the corporate partner's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization as applicable to the jurisdiction of issuance

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board or management resolution authorizing the contribution to the SCSp, designating the representative and accepting the partnership agreement
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the corporate General Partner or the relevant governing body
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified extract countersigned by the corporate secretary, followed by Hague Apostille / consular legalization per the jurisdiction of the issuer

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming source of funds, business profile and expected transactional activity of the B2B enterprise SaaS operation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed financial institution holding the ultimate investors' funds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original banker's letter bearing the bank's wet signature and official seal, countersigned and authenticated by notary, then Hague Apostille / consular legalization per the bank's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address of each individual UBO (utility bill dated within the last three months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider (electricity, water, gas, or telecom) or public registry of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified notarial copy in the country of origin followed by Hague Apostille / consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Professional curriculum vitae or corporate profile of the General Partner and of the intended manager responsible for the SaaS business decisions in Luxembourg
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Proposed General Partner (self-issued) or supervisory/regulated body in the partner's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in the country of origin followed by Hague Apostille / consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn French translation of every non-French document in the bundle
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Sworn translator admitted before the Luxembourg courts (traducteur assermenté)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Translator's signed certification; notarial exemplification (certificat de conformité) when required by the RCS, RBE or the banking institution

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, General Partners, directors, beneficiaries and authorized signatories against (i) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, (ii) the UN Security Council Consolidated List, (iii) the OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, and (iv) the Luxembourg national asset-freezing list maintained by the Ministry of Finance. Where a Politically Exposed Person (PEP), family member or close associate is identified, enhanced due diligence is applied in accordance with Article 3-5 of the amended Law of 12 November 2004 and FATF Recommendation 12. Any positive hit, discrepancy in source of funds, or high-risk jurisdiction nexus triggers a mandatory Suspicious Transaction Report (STR) to the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (Cellule de Renseignement Financier - CRF) under Article 5(2) of the 2004 AML Law.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - electronic one-stop-shop for the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) at www.lbr.lu; preliminary name availability is assessed via the LBR interlocutory search and validated at the time of formal electronic filing
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Official filings are accepted in French, German or Luxembourgish, with French serving as the working language of the RCS. The company name must be expressed in Latin characters; non-Latin names (Cyrillic, CJK, Arabic) must be presented in a standard romanized transliteration for registration. Article 1023-1 of the Law of 10 August 1915 mandates that an SCSp name include the words 'Société en Commandite Spéciale' or the acronym 'SCSp'. The name must be distinguishable from all existing registered names and must not mislead as to legal form, corporate object, or affiliation with any public or sovereign entity.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: LUXEMBOURG / LETZEBUERG (as a standalone corporate denominator without distinctive additional element)
BANQUE / BANK / CREDIT (requires prior CSSF banking licence)
ASSURANCE / REASSURANCE (requires prior CAA insurance licence)
BOURSE / STOCK EXCHANGE / TRADING PLATFORM (requires prior CSSF/MFSA recognition)
FONDS / FUND / OPC / OPCVM (invokes regulated investment fund terminology)
ETAT / GOUVERNEMENT / MINISTERE / COMMUNE / ADMINISTRATION (false sovereign connotation)
EUROPE / UNION EUROPEENNE (protected EU symbols and denominations)
NOTAIRE / AVOCAT / REVISEUR / CABINET JURIDIQUE (regulated professions requiring prior professional title authorization)
CHAMBRE / ORDRE / INSTITUT (reserved for chartered or professional bodies)
SA / SARL / SCA / SCS / SECS (protected statutory forms not matching the SCSp legal form)
SCSP / SPF / SOPARFI (reserved statutory abbreviations protected for specific entity types)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The Luxembourg RCS does not operate a stand-alone public pre-registration reservation system; the name is secured at filing. Upon any provisional objection or formal rejection by the LBR Registrar: (i) the applicant obtains the Registrar's written reasons; (ii) an amended name may be resubmitted immediately for a fresh 30-day clearance cycle; (iii) a formal administrative contestation may be filed before the President of the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg) in summary proceedings within two months of notification, with mandatory representation by an avocat à la Cour; (iv) the Court either orders the RCS to effect registration or refuses the order; (v) an appeal lies to the Court of Cassation within one month of the ruling.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Acceptable subject to conditions - an SCSp may register at the premises of a licensed domiciliation agent (law firm, fiduciary, or professional support entity) physically situated in Luxembourg. Under Circular LIR 47/1 - 59/3bis of 12 May 2020 and BEPS Action 5 principles, the registered office address must be supported by proportionate economic substance: day-to-day management, decision-taking on contracts, invoicing and cash management, and coherent administrative resources dedicated to the B2B enterprise SaaS activity. A pure letterbox arrangement is insufficient for tax, VAT, banking, or payment-rail (Stripe Billing, Wise B2B) onboarding purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate - approximately 8% per annum during the first 24 months of operation. Unannounced physical on-site inspections by the Luxembourg direct tax administration or RBE supervision are atypical for a low-risk enterprise SaaS vehicle without local staff, but announced document-based substance audits accompanying corporate tax and VAT filings are routine. If the SCSp records additional substance triggers, such as a local director in the tax-exempt regime or registration for withholding VAT, the probability of a desk audit increases to a still-manageable 15-20% per annum.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Luxembourg name clearance and LBR preliminary non-confusion search
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) and/or licensed fiduciary
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed statutory search and extract fee of the LBR; prevailing market benchmark for electronic name clearance

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of SCSp partnership agreement (contrat de société), UBO piercing memorandum and AML/KYC onboarding pack
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Boutique Luxembourg law firm or licensed PFS legal department
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market fixed fee for an international SCSp formation with UBO analysis; blended hourly rate EUR 350-500 for a 8-10 hour engagement

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial deed of formation (when structured as notarial act) and notary AML/compliance verifications
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg notaire (Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff regulated by Grand-Ducal Regulation of 29 May 2009; fixed minimum deed fee scaled to the contribution schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS registration and legal publication in the Recueil Electronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Ministry of Justice (RESA)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed statutory RCS filing fee under Article 34 of the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 23 January 2003, plus the mandatory electronic publication tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration of UBO declaration in the RBE register (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No filing fee is chargeable; filing is mandatory within one month of RCS registration under the Law of 13 January 2019

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Domiciliation and registered office services, first full year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed fiduciary, PFS or professional domiciliation agent supervised by the CSSF
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Annual market tariff for a CSSF-compliant Luxembourg domiciliation with registered correspondence handling and administrative screening

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization, Hague Apostille and consular legalization bundle for the UBO/General Partner identity and corporate documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Ministry of Foreign Affairs, foreign competent Apostille authorities, and Luxembourg embassies/consulates (where consular legalization is required)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Blended fixed administrative fee per instrument across up to six jurisdictions, based on prevailing consular tariffs and Apostille schedules

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn translations of corporate and UBO documents into French (and where necessary German/English)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn translator admitted before the Luxembourg courts
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official per-page/per-word tariff of the Luxembourg Bar/Ministry of Justice for sworn legal translations; estimated 15-20 pages

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Administrative, courier, expedited mail and agent signing fees
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Various (international courier, signing agents, power-of-attorney exemplification)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Out-of-pocket benchmark for secure document transmission and signature certification outside Luxembourg

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, particularly Articles 32-1 to 32-9 (Société en Commandite Spéciale), together with the Law of 19 December 2002 on the Trade and Companies Register and company accounts.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) through the eJustice / MyGuichet portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts (Articles of Association / Partnership Agreement) filed electronically for registration with the RCS and publication in the RESA.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum capital or escrow account requirement; the SCSp may be constituted with zero capital and partner subscriptions may be in cash or in kind.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the General Partner, acting for the SCSp, hereby adopts the initial resolutions for the Société en Commandite Spéciale. It acknowledges and subscribes the partnership interests in accordance with the executed partnership agreement. The registered office is established at [Address], Luxembourg, with a registered agent confirmed. The General Partner appoints [Name] as manager/authorized representative and the Professional Partner as compliance officer. All persons are authorized to execute the RCS filing, any declarations before notaries and trade registers, and to open bank accounts and retain service providers for the sole purpose of completing registration and licensing formalities. This resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Optional Notarization of the Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Partner (internal act); optional Luxembourg notary for private deed form
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the statuts (partnership agreement) identifying the general partner and limited partners, registered office address, corporate object (enterprise cloud software development), profit sharing, and governance. Execute the agreement in private writing or before a notary. No minimum capital certificate is required. If a real property lease is registered, notarial form may be required.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS objects to a statutory clause, call a general partner meeting to amend the statuts and resubmit for registration; no monetary penalty if corrected within the regulatory deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Name Reservation Module (MyGuichet)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search the RCS index to confirm the intended corporate name is available and does not conflict with existing protected names. Reserve the name and verify that its suffix includes 'SCSp' or 'Société en Commandite Spéciale'.
required_dossiers: Certificate of non-conflicting name issued by LBR
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, adopt a secondary proposed name and resubmit without additional cost within the same filing session.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via Luxembourg Business Registers / eJustice Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed statuts, partner identification, registered office consent, and general partner resolution through the LBR electronic data room. Pay the official filing fee online. The RCS examines legality and issues the RCS registration number.
required_dossiers: First board resolution of general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, provide the requested clarifications or amend the statuts; if rejected, correct the file and resubmit with the applicable fee or appeal the refusal before the Luxembourg commercial court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Electronic Compendium and Legal Effect
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, the registry automatically arranges publication of the statutory excerpt in the RESA. Verify that all mandatory legal mentions are present and that the date of legal effectiveness is correctly recorded.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a publication typographical error occurs, submit a rectification request to the RCS; no fee is charged if the request is made within five working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appointment of Officers and Operational Readiness
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt the first board resolution approving the subscription of partnership interests, appointing the manager/authorized representatives, and confirming the registered agent. Open the corporate bank account and prepare the active launch of the B2B SaaS commercial contracts.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or a counterparty requests additional corporate details, amend the first board resolution or issue a certificate of incumbency from the registered agent.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for ISIC 6201 enterprise cloud software; reference only: Luxembourg Ministry of the Economy – Direction générale de la propriété intellectuelle and, for physical office premises, the competent commune business authorization may apply.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable – no industrial or commercial operating license is required for the development and provision of enterprise SaaS software services.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not required; office-only software development activities are outside the mandatory EIA listing in the Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental assessment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Office operations only: comply with municipal waste sorting and collection, WEEE electrical waste disposal, energy performance reporting of the leased premises, and municipal wastewater discharge rules; no industrial VOC or process wastewater emission thresholds apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification for the leased office premises in accordance with the commune fire department; occupational workplace clearance under the Labour Code, including health and safety audits, first aid equipment, and evacuation signage; no civil defense industrial permit is required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT. Official digital portals: MyGuichet.lu (eTVA, eCDF, and online RCS filings) and Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) via lbr.lu for commercial registry filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Execute the SCSp partnership agreement (private deed is sufficient absent contributions of registered real estate; a notarial instrument is commonly used for Luxembourg registered-office formalities). Step 2: File the registration dossier with the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) through the single point of contact on MyGuichet.lu; obtain the RCS registration number, the STATEC national business number (numéro de matricule national), and the commercial register excerpt. Step 3: Publish the required notice in the electronic official gazette (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations, RESA) and file the beneficial-owner declaration with the Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE) within one month of registration. Step 4: Register for VAT with the AEDT using the VAT registration form (Formulaire 640) submitted via MyGuichet.lu; obtain the Luxembourg VAT identification number (format LU + 8 digits), which is synchronised with the RCS identification; registration must be completed before the first taxable transaction is performed or invoiced. Step 5: Maintain the statutory corporate and tax files at the registered office, file the annual RCS confirmation (confirmation annuelle), and keep current the RBE register.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible. The SCSp is fiscally transparent by statutory rule for Luxembourg direct taxes (income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax are not levied at the partnership level); each general or limited partner is taxed directly on its allocated share of SaaS profits as if the profits had been realised by that partner, subject to treaty protection in cross-border structures. The partnership remains a taxable person (assujetti) for VAT purposes where it acts in its own name in an independent economic activity. Territorial scope: the SCSp is a Luxembourg-resident pass-through entity with its registered office and place of actual management in Luxembourg; there is no sub-state tax layer in the Grand Duchy.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not apply a US-style check-the-box system; the transparent status of the SCSp is automatic and cannot be overridden for direct tax purposes. Available elections include: (i) fiscal unity (intégration fiscale) under Article 164bis LIR for a corporate partner holding directly or indirectly at least 95% of the capital of one or more Luxembourg resident companies, with no election available at the SCSp level itself; (ii) VAT group election (assujetti unique) under Article 60 of the Luxembourg VAT law where the SCSp is established in Luxembourg and has financial, economic, and organisational links with other group members, allowing a single VAT filing group; (iii) the small business exemption option (franchise d'imposition) under Article 57 of the VAT law where annual turnover does not exceed EUR 35,000, which is generally not advisable for an exporting SaaS business because it forfeits input VAT deduction; (iv) no separate hybrid mismatch election exists, but Luxembourg applies the ATAD-compliant hybrid rules (law of 21 December 2018 and subsequent amendments) that deny deductions for payments that are deductible in Luxembourg and not correspondingly taxed or included in income elsewhere.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (TVA - Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée), implemented under EU Directive 2006/112/EC and the Luxembourg VAT law (Loi TVA).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover (excluding VAT) for the domestic small business exemption; however, a B2B SaaS operator is obliged to register for Luxembourg VAT from the first taxable transaction in Luxembourg when it is established in Luxembourg or when it intends to perform cross-border B2B services subject to reverse charge, because no general threshold applies for obtaining a VAT number to validate reverse-charge neutrality, file EC Sales Lists, and exercise input VAT deduction; the registration must be completed before invoicing or performance of the external supply.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not currently operate a real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control (CTC), or digital stamping regime for B2B electronic invoicing. B2G e-invoicing has been mandatory for public contracts above the relevant thresholds via the PEPPOL network since 1 January 2024. B2B e-invoicing remains voluntary and PEPPOL/UBL formats are accepted; no AEDT real-time API validation or reporting obligation applies in the B2B channel as of the current legal position. Mandatory B2B e-reporting and e-invoicing are expected only after the transposition of the EU VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) package, currently projected for the 2027-2030 horizon. The SCSp must nonetheless issue compliant invoices through Stripe Billing or Wise B2B, follow statutory invoice dating and content rules, and file Luxembourg VAT returns monthly or quarterly through the eTVA portal.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: B2B Enterprise SaaS supplied by the Luxembourg SCSp to non-resident business customers qualifies for the territoriality override under Article 44 of Directive 2006/112/EC, under which the place of supply is the customer's establishment rather than Luxembourg. Supplies to EU business customers are outside Luxembourg VAT and subject to reverse charge in the customer's member state; supplies to non-EU business customers are effectively zero-rated in Luxembourg. Eligibility requires (i) a valid customer VAT identification number for EU customers, (ii) documentary evidence of the customer's establishment outside Luxembourg, and (iii) contractual and factual demonstration of the business-to-business character of the SaaS licence. The zero-rated export supplies preserve the pro-rata right of input VAT deduction, so VAT on cloud hosting, software development, legal, and professional fees remains fully reclaimable to the extent attributable to export turnover.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Executed B2B SaaS master subscription agreement and order forms evidencing the customer's business identity, establishment country, and licence scope
Customer VAT identification number (EU customers) or certificate of tax residence / foreign company registration extract (non-EU customers) retained per customer file
Inward remittance evidence: Stripe Billing and Wise B2B settlement reports, bank account credit receipts, or SWIFT/MT103 confirmations covering the invoiced amount
Service delivery and usage records (hosting logs, user activity reports, server access records) demonstrating that the SaaS application was made available to the non-resident customer

Luxembourg VAT returns and EC Sales Lists (EU customers) showing the value of the export supplies and, where any ancillary goods are supplied with the service, supporting transport or customs evidence
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT may reassess VAT retroactively for five years (ten years in cases of fraudulent declaration) under Article 76 of the Luxembourg VAT law; if the customer's establishment or the business-to-business substance is not substantiated, the invoiced SaaS fees are recharacterised as taxable Luxembourg supplies and the VAT is clawed back together with default interest at the statutory late payment rate (0.8% per month on unpaid amounts). Misdeclaration and non-compliance penalties range from EUR 250 to EUR 4,000 per offence (Articles 73 and 74 of the VAT law), the tax due may be doubled in cases of deliberate concealment, and criminal conviction for tax fraud may lead to imprisonment of up to five years. Luxembourg tax law does not impose a statutory export FX repatriation deadline, but the 180-day reference period is a customary covenant applied by Luxembourg credit institutions and payment providers (Stripe, Wise) to satisfy foreign-exchange control, sanctions, and AML/CFT expectations; failure to demonstrate repatriation within this window materially increases procedural audit exposure, including risk of reclassification of export turnover and review of related-party financing arrangements.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) in coordination with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) and the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance; monetary and FX policy is delegated to the European Central Bank (ECB) within the Eurosystem. There is no dedicated national foreign exchange administration; BCL supervises balance-of-payments statistics, T2 (TARGET services) and the Luxembourg Interbank Payment System (LIPS), while capital-flow rules follow EU Treaty provisions and the EU/UN financial sanctions framework.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible in Luxembourg. Current and capital account transactions are unrestricted under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and the OECD Code of Liberalisation of Capital Movements. Profit remittances and partner distributions by an SCSp to resident or non-resident partners are generally exempt from Luxembourg withholding tax because the SCSp is fiscally transparent for income tax purposes (subject to substance and no commercial-activity disqualification), and no prior exchange-control approval or conversion permit is required. The only operational requirements are (i) BCL balance-of-payments statistical reporting for cross-border transactions at or above EUR 12,500 per operation, and (ii) mandatory screening against EU consolidated financial sanctions lists; no quantitative limits or remittance delays apply.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender or mandatory conversion ratio exists in Luxembourg. SaaS export receipts under ISIC 6201 may be freely retained in EUR or any foreign currency in Luxembourg bank accounts and can be converted or rebilled through any authorised credit institution. Reporting obligations are limited to BCL balance-of-payments declarations (transaction threshold EUR 12,500, aggregate monthly reporting) and standard EU anti-money-laundering declarations; there is no obligation to sell foreign currency to the central bank or to a domestic bank, and no service-sector Intrastat filing applies.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (SEPA, SWIFT, trade finance links)
Capital Escrow Account (non-resident partner capital wiring)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: High as a collection/billing rail, Medium as the sole treasury or clearing account. Legal constraints: Wise (Wise Europe SA, Belgium-licensed EMI) and Stripe Billing (Stripe Technology Europe Ltd, Ireland-licensed EMI) are EEA payment institutions passporting into Luxembourg under PSD2; they are not credit institutions, cannot accept deposits on their own balance sheet, do not participate in the Luxembourg FGDL deposit-guarantee scheme, and must safeguard client funds in segregated accounts held with an EEA credit institution. For an SCSp, using Wise/Stripe for B2B SaaS revenue intake and business payouts is lawful and operationally efficient, but enterprise counterparties and Luxembourg treasury practice require final settlement through a Luxembourg IBAN; the recommended blueprint is to use Stripe and Wise as charge-and-disbursement rails and sweep balances daily to a Tier-1 Luxembourg bank account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg credit institutions generally require an in-person or bank-approved video-identity interview for at least one general partner (GP) representative or authorised signatory before opening an account for an SCSp; fully remote opening is rarely offered to newly formed, non-resident-owned pass-through entities. The standard mandate includes valid passport or EU national ID, proof of residence, CV and source-of-funds statement, the original or certified copy of the SCSp partnership agreement (private deed or notarial deed), the notarised RBE filing extract, a registered-office or domiciliation agreement in Luxembourg, and a corporate resolution designating signatories. Banks apply the Luxembourg AML Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF Regulation 12-02; remote video onboarding may be accepted where the bank's policy permits and all underlying partners are in OECD or non-high-risk jurisdictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Zero-minimum-capital SCSp with fiscal transparency and no audited financial history, potentially recharacterised as an anonymous shell or unlicensed fund vehicle.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: certified copy of the partnership agreement and management regulations; RBE extract and UBO organisational chart to ultimate natural persons; business plan evidencing enterprise SaaS ARR and employee headcount; documented initial working-capital transfer from a clearly sourced partner account; tax counsel letter confirming transparency classification; and accountant-compiled or audited financial statements for the preceding 12 months.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership with a foreign corporate GP, raising beneficial-ownership opacity, sanctions exposure and substance doubts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: valid passports, residential proof and source-of-wealth statements for all beneficial owners above 25%; corporate registry extracts for the full GP chain in each jurisdiction; signed AML/KYC questionnaire; EU/CSSF sanctions-list screening printouts; and Luxembourg substance documentation including registered-office lease, local administrator appointment minutes and payroll records where applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border SaaS invoices settled via Stripe and Wise without physical goods, increasing the risk of uninvoiced third-party circulation or unreported services.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: executed B2B SaaS subscription contracts; Stripe KYB and Wise business verification reports with invoice-level settlement history; Luxembourg VAT registration evidence covering B2B e-services place-of-supply rules; revenue ledger mapped to ISIC 6201; written no-cash and no-third-party-payout policies; and six months of bank statements from the fintech rails showing consistent, low-risk recurring billing.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections must be wired via SWIFT MT103 (or SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR) from a fully KYC'd partner bank, referencing 'Capital contribution under Article [X] of the SCSp partnership agreement'. Include BCL/ECB balance-of-payments code 409 (Direct Investment - Equity Capital) or code 484 for financial/fund flows when the beneficiary bank requests the statistical code; reference the Luxembourg IBAN and attach a signed capital contribution letter with a UBO declaration so the receiving bank can reconcile source of funds. No exchange-control permit is required, but transactions of EUR 12,500 or more are reported to the BCL for balance-of-payments statistics. For SaaS subscription revenue, non-resident B2B customers settle via Stripe Billing using code 211 (Computer services) in BCL statistics; funds sweep from the EMI safeguarding account to the Luxembourg operating account via SEPA; USD revenue arrives through the bank's nostro correspondent and is auto-converted to EUR through a disclosed spot trade.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade and corporate disbursements use SWIFT MT103 for foreign-currency wires, SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR within the EEA, SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst via TIPS or RT1) for sub-EUR 100,000 urgent payments, and T2/LIPS for large-value same-day EUR clearing. Commercial letters of credit (UCP 600) and documentary collections are available through BIL and BGL BNP Paribas for trade settlements, although SaaS exports generally require only Peppol/UBL e-invoicing matched to the payment instruction. Each outbound payment must reference the underlying commercial invoice and pre-verified beneficiary KYB record, and every wire is screened against EU/CSSF sanctions lists before release.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD Outright Forwards (deliverable vanilla FX forwards in standard tenors)
EUR/USD FX Swaps and rolled spot contracts for intra-treasury liquidity conversion
FX options and zero-cost collars on liquid G10 pairs (European-style plain-vanilla structures)
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on restricted currencies such as USD/CNH, USD/BRL and USD/IDR transacted as offshore contracts with regulated Luxembourg banks
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) and long-dated cross-currency swaps under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement, cleared through LCH SwapClear or Eurex Clearing with CSSF/ESMA trade reporting

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of registered corporate data (confirmation annuelle)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Between 1 January and 31 March of each calendar year; mandatory annual filing for all registered civil and commercial entities.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal reminder from RCS, administrative late-filing penalties up to EUR 500, and risk of eventual judicial dissolution / strike-off from the register for persistent non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial owner (UBO) re-confirmation and update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs / RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Co-filed with the annual confirmation (1 January to 31 March); any change in SCSp partners or beneficial ownership must additionally be filed within one month of the event.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fines up to EUR 150,000 in less serious cases, up to EUR 1,250,000 and/or imprisonment for wilful non-disclosure, together with possible deregistration proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing (conditional for SCSp undertakings meeting size or opt-in thresholds)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of the financial year-end given a standard 31 December year-end; if annual accounts are voluntarily disclosed, within 1 month of approval by the partners.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court-ordered filing, administrative fines up to EUR 10,000, and potential civil liability of the general partner/manager for failure to disclose.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual income tax declaration (transparent partnership return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD), Luxembourg Direct Tax Authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year SCSp, due by 31 December of the year immediately following the tax year; electronic-filing practices and tax-office published grace periods apply.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of 10% of assessed partnership tax liability, minimum EUR 150; increased penalties 20% after formal notice; monthly late-interest accrual at EUR 0.6% until payment.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit by an approved réviseur d'entreprises where the SCSp exceeds two of three thresholds at balance-sheet date: balance-sheet total > EUR 4,400,000, net turnover > EUR 8,800,000, or average full-time workforce > 50; audit also required when the SCSp is subject to regulation as an alternative investment fund (AIF) under CSSF supervision.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (annual accounts directive-compliant); IFRS as endorsed by the EU permitted for consolidated or voluntarily adopted annual financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The RCS annual confirmation incorporates a mandatory re-confirmation of beneficial-owner data. An SCSp must record any transfer, assignment, or economic-interest change in its partners and beneficial-ownership register, filing the update with LBR within one month of the transaction; the annual 1 January–31 March filing re-confirms the existing UBO details for the register.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of General Partners / Managers (Registre des gérants commandités)
Minute Book of Partner Resolutions and Decisions

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (Luxembourg City aggregate rate: CIT 17% + solidarity surcharge 7% + municipal business tax ~6.75%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP box regime: 80% deduction on qualifying IP income, effective rate ~5%. Participation exemption for dividends and capital gains. Notional interest deduction (NID) for equity increases.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 510 (Corporate Income Tax Return) – used for SCSp as a transparency declaration; filed electronically via MyGuichet.lu or eTax
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 31 May following the fiscal year-end, extendable to 31 December upon justified request

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification of the SCSp (name, address, RCS number)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide Luxembourg RCS number and local tax representative details if applicable

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year start and end dates
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Indicate the exact period covered by the return
Report worldwide income attributable to Luxembourg source activities; for non-resident partners, only Luxembourg-source income is relevant

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses (operating costs, depreciation, interest, royalties)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure expenses are arm's length and properly documented; non-resident partners must allocate expenses proportionally

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income (or loss) before allocation to partners
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This amount is allocated to each partner according to their profit-sharing ratio

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of income to partners (name, address, tax ID, share percentage)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List each partner's share; non-resident partners must provide their tax residency and TRC if claiming treaty benefits

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits and prepayments (e.g., foreign tax credits, withholding tax credits)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners may claim foreign tax credits on their home country return, not on the Luxembourg return

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: €250 to €2,500; late payment interest: 0.6% per month on unpaid tax; additional penalties for gross negligence or fraud up to 100% of tax due

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% (standard) – but SCSp is fiscally transparent; distributions to partners are not subject to Luxembourg withholding tax. If the SCSp is treated as opaque (e.g., via check-the-box election), the 15% rate applies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced WHT under a DTA, the beneficial owner must submit a tax residency certificate (TRC) from their home jurisdiction and file Form 270 (or Form 271 for refunds) with the Luxembourg tax authority (ACD). The TRC must be certified and include the relevant tax year. Processing typically takes 3-6 months.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 15%; reduced to 0% under EU Interest & Royalties Directive if conditions met (beneficial owner is EU resident, 25%+ shareholding, etc.). Interest: statutory 15%; often exempt under domestic law for interest paid to EU/EEA residents or under DTA (typically 0-10%).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File required if related-party transactions exceed €450,000 (goods or services) or €100,000 for financial transactions; Master File required if group consolidated revenue exceeds €50 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg applies Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) for certain activities (e.g., financing, IP holding). For SaaS, general substance requirements apply to avoid being classified as a shell company. The SCSp must demonstrate adequate staff, premises, and decision-making in Luxembourg if it claims treaty benefits or engages in intra-group transactions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate underreporting of income, false deductions, or artificial transfer pricing arrangements to shift profits to low-tax jurisdictions without economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fines up to €250,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years; civil penalties up to 100% of tax evaded; interest on unpaid tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held personally liable for unpaid taxes if they knowingly participated in evasion; travel bans and asset freezes may be imposed; potential extradition for cross-border fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a shell with no real economic activity, no employees, no physical presence, and no substantive business purpose, solely to obtain tax benefits or treaty shopping.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, reclassification of income, imposition of 15% WHT on distributions, and potential liquidation; fines up to €50,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for unpaid taxes and penalties if they knowingly allowed the company to operate as a shell; potential criminal charges for fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to conduct customer due diligence, reporting suspicious transactions, or maintaining adequate records for B2B SaaS payments, especially involving high-risk jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to €1 million or 10% of annual turnover; criminal penalties for money laundering up to 5 years imprisonment; freezing of assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers can be personally fined and imprisoned for AML violations; travel bans and prohibition from holding directorship may be imposed.
